preconditions.expression: t == int(stdin.split()[0]) and t >= 1 and t <= 1000
preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 1000) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(2 <= int(line) <= 200000 for line in stdin.split()[1::2])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line after t is an integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 2e5) representing the number of people.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(a) <= 200000 for a in stdin.split()[2::2])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the second line contains n space-separated integers a_i (0 ≤ a_i ≤ 2e5) representing sociability parameters.
The sum of all a_i across all test cases does not exceed 2e5.

postconditions.description: For each test case, the first line of output is an integer k representing the maximum number of talks possible.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(i) <= n and 1 <= int(j) <= n and int(i) != int(j) for line in stdout.split()[1:] for i, j in [line.split()])
postconditions.description: Each subsequent line contains two integers i and j (1 ≤ i, j ≤ n and i ≠ j) representing pairs of people who talk.
The total number of talks k is maximized, where max_possible_talks(a) is the maximum possible number of talks given the sociability array a.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= a_i - count_talks_for_person(i, talks) <= 0 for i in range(1, n+1))
postconditions.description: For each person i, the number of talks they participate in does not exceed their sociability a_i, where talks is the list of talk pairs.
